You said:
Which iPhone apps let me see iCloud, Google and Outlook calendars together? Distinguish a combined view from copying busy time between accounts, and cite official sources for the products you recommend.
ChatGPT said:

Yes. Several iPhone calendar apps can display iCloud, Google Calendar, and Microsoft Outlook calendars together in one view, without moving or duplicating your events.

The important distinction is between two very different features:

Combined calendar view: One app displays events from all three accounts, usually with different colors. The events remain in their original calendars, and changes sync back to the appropriate account.

Busy-time synchronization: A service copies or mirrors your availability between accounts, often by creating private “Busy” blocks. This helps prevent double-booking when someone checks only one of your calendars, but it is not necessary simply to see all your appointments together.

For your stated goal, I would start with Apple Calendar or Fantastical.

Best iPhone apps for all three calendars

1. Apple Calendar — Best free option

Built into iPhone. Displays iCloud, Google, Outlook.com, and Microsoft Exchange calendars together. You can show or hide individual calendars and choose which account receives new events.

Combined view: Yes · Busy-time copying: No

Apple's setup instructions · Microsoft's Outlook instructions

2. Fantastical — Best premium calendar experience

Supports iCloud, Google, Exchange, and Microsoft 365 directly. Offers flexible calendar views, calendar sets, natural-language event entry, and more advanced scheduling features. Some features require a subscription.

Combined view: Yes · Busy-time copying: Not required

Official compatibility FAQ · Account setup guide

3. Calendars by Readdle — Strong alternative

Direct connections for iCloud, Google, Outlook, and Exchange. Readdle explicitly confirms that events from connected calendars appear in one unified, color-coded view, with edits synced to their respective services.

Combined view: Yes · Busy-time copying: No

Official account and unified-view guide

4. Microsoft Outlook — Best if you already work in Outlook

The Outlook iPhone app can display Microsoft, Google, and iCloud calendars together. Microsoft explicitly documents adding an iCloud account to Outlook so its events appear alongside other calendars.

Combined view: Yes · Busy-time copying: No

Microsoft's iCloud integration guide · Supported calendar accounts

Combined view vs. busy-time synchronization

These features solve different problems.

A second event blocks the same time in another account.

A combined view lets you see that you're occupied. It doesn't necessarily let a colleague scheduling through Outlook see that you're busy with a personal Google or iCloud appointment.

Busy-time synchronization is useful when you need that second capability. It may require a separate calendar-sync service, additional permissions, and careful privacy settings.

Note: Workplace Microsoft 365 accounts can restrict third-party calendar access through organizational security policies. Check with your IT administrator if an account cannot be added.

How to get started with Apple Calendar

You may not need to install anything.

Open Settings → Apps → Calendar → Calendar Accounts.

Add your Google account and enable Calendars.

Add Outlook.com for a personal Microsoft account, or Microsoft Exchange for an appropriate work account.

Make sure iCloud Calendar is enabled.

Open Apple Calendar, tap Calendars, and select all the calendars you want visible.

Apple and Microsoft both document these setup steps.

My recommendation: Use Apple Calendar first. Try Fantastical if you want a more sophisticated interface, or Readdle Calendars if you prefer another dedicated calendar app.

One question that could change the recommendation: Do you only want to see all three calendars together on your iPhone, or do you also need your Outlook colleagues to see you as busy when you have an appointment in iCloud or Google?
